# Discrete Distributions

## Bernoulli Distribution
A single trial where the outcome is success (1) or failure (0).

#### Parameter
- **p**: probability of success

#### Probability Mass Function

$$
P(X = x) =
\begin{cases}
p & (x = 1) \\
1-p & (x = 0)
\end{cases}
$$

#### Mean & Variance

$$
E[X] = p, \quad Var[X] = p(1-p)
$$


```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center

from scipy.stats import bernoulli
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

p = 0.3
x = [0, 1]
pmf = bernoulli.pmf(x, p)

plt.bar(x, pmf, width=0.3)
plt.title("Bernoulli(p=0.3)")
plt.xlabel("x")
plt.ylabel("P(X=x)")
plt.xticks([0,1])
plt.show()
```

#### Examples
- Coin toss (heads vs tails)
- Customer clicks an advertisement
- Product purchase (yes/no)


## Binomial Distribution
Counts the number of successes in n independent Bernoulli trials.

#### Parameters
- **n**: number of trials
- **p**: probability of success in each trial

#### Probability Mass Function

$$
P(X = k) = \binom{n}{k} p^k (1-p)^{n-k}
$$

#### Mean & Variance

$$
E[X] = np, \quad Var[X] = np(1-p)
$$

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center

from scipy.stats import binom
import numpy as np

n, p = 10, 0.3
x = np.arange(0, n+1)
pmf = binom.pmf(x, n, p)

plt.bar(x, pmf, width=0.3)
plt.title("Binomial Distribution (n=10, p=0.3)")
plt.xlabel("k")
plt.ylabel("P(X=k)")
plt.show()
```

#### Examples
- Number of customers who purchase out of 10
- Number of defective products in a batch
- Basketball free-throw successes


## Poisson Distribution
Counts the number of events in a fixed time or space interval.

#### Parameter
- **λ**: average event rate per interval

#### Probability Mass Function

$$
P(X = k) = \frac{\lambda^k e^{-\lambda}}{k!}
$$

#### Mean & Variance

$$
E[X] = \lambda, \quad Var[X] = \lambda
$$

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center

from scipy.stats import poisson

lam = 3
x = np.arange(0, 15)
pmf = poisson.pmf(x, lam)

plt.bar(x, pmf, width=0.3)
plt.title("Poisson Distribution (λ=3)")
plt.xlabel("k")
plt.ylabel("P(X=k)")
plt.show()
```

#### Examples
- Calls received by a call center in 1 hour
- Number of earthquakes per year
- Number of emails per minute


## Geometric Distribution
Number of trials needed until the first success.

#### Parameter
- **p**: probability of success per trial

#### Probability Mass Function

$$
P(X = k) = (1-p)^{k-1} p
$$

Mean & Variance

$$
E[X] = \frac{1}{p}, \quad Var[X] = \frac{1-p}{p^2}
$$

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center

from scipy.stats import geom

p = 0.3
x = np.arange(1, 15)
pmf = geom.pmf(x, p)

plt.bar(x, pmf, width=0.3)
plt.title("Geometric Distribution (p=0.3)")
plt.xlabel("Trials")
plt.ylabel("P(X=k)")
plt.show()
```

#### Examples
- Number of coin tosses until first heads
- Attempts until first customer purchases
- Inspections until first defective product


## Negative Binomial Distribution
Number of trials needed until r successes occur.

#### Parameters
- **r**: required number of successes
- **p**: probability of success

#### Probability Mass Function

$$
P(X = k) = \binom{k-1}{r-1} (1-p)^{k-r} p^r
$$

#### Mean & Variance

$$
E[X] = \frac{r}{p}, \quad Var[X] = \frac{r(1-p)}{p^2}
$$

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center

from scipy.stats import nbinom

r, p = 3, 0.3
x = np.arange(r, r+20)
pmf = nbinom.pmf(x-r, r, p)

plt.bar(x, pmf, width=0.3)
plt.title("Negative Binomial Distribution (r=3, p=0.3)")
plt.xlabel("Trials")
plt.ylabel("P(X=k)")
plt.show()
```

#### Examples
- Customers until 5 purchases occur
- Number of shots until scoring 3 goals
- Failures until a product breaks multiple times


# Continuous Distributions

## Normal Distribution
A common continuous distribution for natural variations.

#### Parameters
- **μ**: mean
- **σ²**: variance

#### Probability Density Function

$$
f(x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi\sigma^{2}}}
\exp\left( -\frac{(x-\mu)^2}{2\sigma^2} \right)
$$

#### Mean & Variance

$$
E[X] = \mu, \quad Var[X] = \sigma^2
$$

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center

from scipy.stats import norm

mu, sigma = 0, 1
x = np.linspace(-4, 4, 400)
pdf = norm.pdf(x, mu, sigma)

plt.plot(x, pdf)
plt.title("Normal Distribution (μ=0, σ=1)")
plt.show()
```

#### Examples

- Height, weight, IQ
- Exam scores


## Exponential Distribution
Waiting time between Poisson events.

#### Parameter
- **λ**: rate parameter (events per unit time)

#### Probability Density Function
$$
f(x) = \lambda e^{-\lambda x}, \quad x \ge 0
$$

#### Mean & Variance
$$
E[X] = \frac{1}{\lambda}, \quad Var[X] = \frac{1}{\lambda^2}
$$


```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center

from scipy.stats import expon

lam = 1
x = np.linspace(0, 10, 400)
pdf = expon.pdf(x, scale=1/lam)

plt.plot(x, pdf)
plt.title("Exponential Distribution (λ=1)")
plt.show()
```

Examples

- Time until next customer arrives
- Time until next machine failure
- Time until radioactive decay


## Gamma Distribution
Time until the k-th event occurs.

#### Parameters
- **k**: shape parameter
- **λ**: rate parameter

#### Probability Density Function

$$
f(x)=\frac{\lambda^{k} x^{k-1} e^{-\lambda x}}{\Gamma(k)}
$$

#### Mean & Variance
$$
E[X] = \frac{\alpha}{\lambda}, \quad Var[X] = \frac{\alpha}{\lambda^2}
$$

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center

from scipy.stats import gamma

k, lam = 3, 1
x = np.linspace(0, 15, 400)
pdf = gamma.pdf(x, a=k, scale=1/lam)

plt.plot(x, pdf)
plt.title("Gamma Distribution (k=3, λ=1)")
plt.show()
```

#### Examples
- Total wait time for multiple arrivals
- Insurance claim modeling
- Bayesian prior for rates


## Chi-Square Distribution
Sum of squared standard normal random variables.

#### Parameter
- **k**: degrees of freedom

#### Definition

$$
X = Z_1^2 + Z_2^2 + \cdots + Z_k^2
$$

$$
f(x)= \frac{1}{2^{k/2}\Gamma(k/2)} x^{k/2 - 1} e^{-x/2}, \quad x \ge 0
$$

#### Mean & Variance
$$
E[X] = k, \quad Var[X] = 2k
$$

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center

from scipy.stats import chi2

df = 5
x = np.linspace(0, 20, 400)
pdf = chi2.pdf(x, df)

plt.plot(x, pdf)
plt.title("Chi-Square Distribution (df=5)")
plt.show()
```

#### Examples
- Variance tests
- Goodness-of-fit test
- Independence test in contingency tables


## Student's t-distribution
Used when population variance is unknown (small samples).

#### Parameter
- **df**: degrees of freedom

#### Definition

$$
T = \frac{\overline{X} - \mu}{S / \sqrt{n}}
$$

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center

from scipy.stats import t

df = 10
x = np.linspace(-5, 5, 400)
pdf = t.pdf(x, df)

plt.plot(x, pdf)
plt.title("Student's t-Distribution (df=10)")
plt.show()
```
#### Examples
- One-sample t-test
- Two-sample t-test
- Confidence intervals


## F-distribution
Ratio of two variances.

#### Parameters
- **df1**: numerator df
- **df2**: denominator df

#### Definition

$$
F = \frac{S_1^2 / df_1}{S_2^2 / df_2}
$$

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center

from scipy.stats import f

df1, df2 = 5, 10
x = np.linspace(0, 5, 400)
pdf = f.pdf(x, df1, df2)

plt.plot(x, pdf)
plt.title("F-Distribution (df1=5, df2=10)")
plt.show()
```

#### Examples
- ANOVA
- Comparing two variances
- Regression significance test


## Beta Distribution
A flexible distribution for modeling probabilities.

#### Parameters
- **α**: left-tail shape
- **β**: right-tail shape

#### Probability Definition Function

$$
f(p) = \frac{1}{B(\alpha,\beta)} p^{\alpha - 1} (1 - p)^{\beta - 1}
$$

#### Mean & Variance
$$
E[X] = \frac{\alpha}{\alpha + \beta}, \quad Var[X] = \frac{\alpha\beta}{(\alpha + \beta)^2(\alpha + \beta + 1)}
$$


```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center

from scipy.stats import beta

a, b = 2, 5
x = np.linspace(0, 1, 400)
pdf = beta.pdf(x, a, b)

plt.plot(x, pdf)
plt.title("Beta Distribution (α=2, β=5)")
plt.show()
```
#### Examples
- Bayesian inference
- A/B testing
- Modeling click-through rates



## Relationships Between Distributions

```
Bernoulli → Binomial → Poisson → Normal
    ↑          ↑
  Beta       Gamma
```

```
Normal → Chi-square → t → F
```


## Summary

| Distribution | Type | When to Use |
|------|------|-----------|
| Bernoulli | Discrete | Single success/failure outcome |
| Binomial | Discrete | Number of successes in n trials |
| Poisson | Discrete | Event count in time/space |
| Geometric | Discrete | Trials until first success |
| Normal | Continuous | Natural variations, measurement |
| Exponential | Continuous | Time between events |
| Gamma | Continuous | Time until k events |
| Chi-square | Continuous | Variance & independence tests |
| t | Continuous | Mean inference (small samples) |
| F | Continuous | Comparing variances, ANOVA |
| Beta | Continuous | Modeling probabilities |


## Key Points
- Normal → basis of CLT
- Poisson → rare events per unit time
- Beta → distribution of probability p
- Binomial → Poisson approximation (np = λ)
- Exponential → waiting time
- Chi-square / t / F → hypothesis testing
- Gamma → sum of exponential waiting times
